item.title: Food Security: Abiodun targets 10,000 farmers with subsidised inputs
item.description: Distributes 10 tractors, 1,200 smartphones to farmers Unveils 39 tractors, harvesters, agro-processing facilities Over 160,000 farmers, value-chain operators captured in state database ByClifford Ndujihe Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has stepped up efforts to boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses and improve farmers’ incomes, unveiling a fresh package of subsidised inputs, mechanisation equipment and digital tools targeting 10,000 rice and cassava farmers. The intervention, announced during the 2026 World Food Day celebration in Abeokuta, includes support for 2,000 rice farmers and 8,000 cassava farmers, the distribution of 10 tractors and 1,200 Android phones loaded with agricultural applications. Under the programme, each beneficiary will receive two bags of fertiliser and one bag of urea. Cassava farmers will also get 25 bundles of cassava stems and 10 litres of herbicides each, while rice farmers will receive three litres of herbicides. The state government said beneficiaries would pay 30 per cent of the cost of the inputs, with the government covering the remaining 70 per cent through its partnership with the International Fund for Agricultural Development, IFAD. The initiative is aimed at reducing farmers’ production costs and improving their capacity to increase output amid rising agricultural expenses and concerns over food affordability. Abiodun also disclosed that his administration had procured 39 tractors, four self-propelled harvesters and other agricultural equipment to strengthen mechanised farming across the state. The 1,200 smartphones distributed to farmers are equipped with applications providing weather information, market prices and guidance on improved farming practices. The digital intervention builds on the Ogun State Farmer Information Management System, launched in April 2023. item.title: Ebola: NCDC holds emergency meeting to conclude action plans
item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has convened an emergency meeting and commenced coordinated response activities following the Federal Government’s declaration of an Ebola outbreak in the country. The agency disclosed this in a statement posted on its official X page on Wednesday, saying the meeting brought together its leadership and key partners to coordinate the response. “The first Incident Management Meeting was convened on October 21, 2026, after the Honorable Minister’s official outbreak declaration of Ebola in Nigeria, bringing together leadership and key partners to align on response efforts,” the NCDC said. The agency also announced that its Incident Action Plan was being finalised, while response teams had commenced field operations focusing on surveillance, contact tracing and infection prevention. “The Incident Action Plan is being finalized today; NCDC teams are on the ground conducting case management and response activities, prioritising enhanced surveillance, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and coordinated risk communication,” the statement read. Reaffirming its commitment to containing the outbreak, the agency said, “We remain committed to a timely, coordinated, and evidence-based response to safeguard the health of Nigerians.” The Federal Government confirmed Nigeria’s first Ebola virus disease case on Tuesday after laboratory tests returned positive in the Federal Capital Territory. The patient, a woman who recently travelled from Uganda on an international flight, reportedly received treatment at a private hospital for several days before the infection was confirmed. She has since been placed in isolation. The post Ebola: NCDC holds emergency meeting to conclude action plans appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers. Atiku said the government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment. He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said. Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but the government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20. “During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said. He also questioned the Presidential Task Force announced by Tinubu in June and chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, insisting that medical experts should lead the response. “Political titles cannot trace contacts, equip hospitals or save lives,” Atiku said. The former vice president further alleged that the planned press conference by the Minister of Health on Thursday was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and voting. “The Tinubu administration must not weaponise Ebola to frighten the public, silence its opponents or suppress voter participation. Any public health measure must be backed by clear medical evidence, applied equally and never used as a pretext to interfere with Nigerians’ democratic rights,” he said. Atiku urged the government to account for the N10 billion, protect health workers and trace all contacts, warning against turning a public health emergency into a tool for political suppression. item.description: Experts downplay fears of AI-driven job losses By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Nigeria loses about $850 million, equivalent to ₦1.13 trillion, annually through its reliance on cloud infrastructure provided by a handful of foreign companies, according to research commissioned by global technology philanthropy Luminate. The Chief Executive Officer of Luminate, Melanie Hui, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the Build 2026 Conference, convened by the Nigeria Artificial Intelligence (AI) Collective. In her address, titled “Africa in the Global AI Order: Towards Equitable Ownership and Shared Prosperity,” Hui said the country’s dependence on foreign cloud infrastructure raised questions about digital ownership and the distribution of economic value. “Nigeria, like countries across the world, relies heavily on cloud infrastructure provided by a handful of foreign companies. The research we commissioned estimates that this dependency costs Nigeria around $850 million each year,” she said. Hui stressed that hosting digital infrastructure within a country’s borders did not necessarily translate into ownership or control. “A country does not own its digital future when a data centre merely sits within its borders. I disagree. Safeguards are the allies of progress,” she said. Citing examples of efforts to hold technology companies accountable, she referenced the Nigerian competition authority’s action against Meta over alleged data exploitation and discriminatory practices. She also noted that app-based drivers in Nigeria had secured government recognition for what she described as Africa’s first e-hailing trade union. Hui called for an AI economy rooted in African agency, capabilities and innovation, where prosperity would be measured not only by market size but also by the opportunities and freedoms available to people. Experts Say AI Could Create More Jobs At the conference, technology experts also sought to allay fears that artificial intelligence would lead to widespread job losses, arguing that the technology could create new employment opportunities and improve productivity. Their comments came amid warnings by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank about AI’s potential impact on the global labour market. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva recently described AI as a “slow-moving tsunami” at the “Small AI: More and Better Jobs” event during the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. She said about 40 per cent of jobs globally could be augmented, downgraded or eliminated by the technology. World Bank Group President Ajay Banga, meanwhile, has emphasised the need to ensure that development translates into employment, arguing that AI should improve productivity and support job creation rather than simply replace workers. However, the Chief Executive Officer of Data Science Nigeria, Dr Olubayi Adekanmbi, argued that the overall gains from AI could outweigh the losses. “There is something we call net effect. Some wins and some losses. But by the time you weigh them together, you will realise that the net effect of AI is going to be much more. Because many jobs that never existed before, AI will make them possible,” he said. Adekanmbi maintained that human judgement would remain important even as AI tools became increasingly integrated into professional work. “AI can help in my diagnosis, but the final decision will still come from doctors. So, a doctor can reach out to more people faster because the doctor has used AI. It’s never taking the job of a doctor. That is why everybody must learn AI so that when you learn AI with your current job, you will not lose your job,” he said. He urged workers to acquire AI skills and learn how to apply the technology within their existing professions. Digital Skills Key to Job Creation The Executive Director of the Policy Innovation Centre and host of the Nigeria AI Collective Secretariat, Dr Osasuyi Dirisu, said digital skills development would be critical to creating jobs for Nigeria’s young population. “We have a very young demographic in Nigeria. In order to create jobs at scale, we need to leverage digital technology. We need to leverage digital jobs, and one of the ways to do that is to build digital skills,” she said. Dirisu said young Nigerians needed to be prepared for emerging employment opportunities through training and continuous skills development. She described the Nigeria AI Collective as “a community of practice that is working to build an ethical and inclusive future for AI development in Nigeria.” Experts Address AI-Generated Election Falsehoods The conference also examined concerns over the use of AI to spread misinformation, disinformation and deepfakes ahead of the 2027 general elections. Dirisu said the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), a partner of the Collective, was working to address the threat through election-monitoring labs and media training. Adekanmbi, however, said AI tools could also help Nigerians verify information and counter falsehoods. “Somebody posts something, and you ask Grok, ‘Please confirm,’ Grok can immediately crawl the internet for you and confirm it,” he said. He proposed extending such verification services to Nigerians without internet access through telephone-based systems. “They can use maybe a mobile phone to call a number and say that ‘I heard something,’ and immediately they can get a response telling them that what you heard is not true. item.title: Websites go dark worldwide as AI exposes critical security flaws
item.description: Government agencies and companies around the world shut down websites Wednesday after two critical flaws came to light involving PHP, a programming language that is the basis for a large share of the internet. The US National Security Agency told organizations to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline. The flaws “often provide a direct path to the server’s file system or database,” the NSA said in a statement on X. Attackers could use them to take over web servers without needing a password. PHP sits underneath popular web design platforms so the weaknesses potentially affect a vast range of websites, from online stores and news outlets to government services. The discovery came amid a surge in software security disclosures driven by increasingly powerful AI models, with the number of vulnerabilities found in 2026 on track to roughly double last year’s record total. PHP volunteers released a fix on Wednesday. “If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now,” the PHP Foundation, which funds developers working on the language, said in a blog post. The flaws were reported in August by security firm Calif and by ChatGPT maker OpenAI, which flagged them independently on the same day. Google-owned cloud security company Wiz later reported further ways to exploit them. The flaws had been reported privately to PHP’s developers at the time and kept confidential while a fix was prepared. Details leaked online Tuesday, a day before the planned release, prompting the rush to take sites offline. In France, local government websites, including the Paris Police Prefecture, have been inaccessible since Wednesday afternoon at the request of the French National Cybersecurity Agency, following “detection of a critical security vulnerability,” the Ministry of the Interior said. In the Netherlands, the national digital identity service DigiD, the website of the House of Representatives and the site of the national cybersecurity center went offline as a precaution, according to Dutch public broadcaster NOS. Belgium’s foreign ministry temporarily took its websites offline as a precaution, it said on X, although the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium had recorded no attacks on Belgian sites. item.title: Reps urge FG to resolve BEDC dispute, restore power
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Government to intervene in the dispute between the National Union of Electricity Employees (NUEE) and the Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC) to restore electricity supply to Edo, Delta, Ondo and Ekiti states. The House warned that the prolonged disruption could endanger lives, cripple essential services and worsen the economic challenges facing residents and businesses in the affected states. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent national importance sponsored by Clement Jimbo, a member of the House from Akwa Ibom State. Presenting the motion, Jimbo expressed concern that the dispute had disrupted electricity supply and forced some critical services to shut down, warning that a prolonged blackout could undermine healthcare delivery, water supply, telecommunications, banking and educational activities. “The disruption of electricity supply over 24 hours, if sustained, poses a serious threat to public safety, socio-economic activities and the delivery of essential services across the affected states,” he said. Jimbo warned that the outage could also disrupt medical services in hospitals, laboratories, maternity centres and emergency units, particularly facilities dependent on electricity to operate life-support equipment and preserve temperature-sensitive medical supplies. He added that small businesses and public infrastructure reliant on regular electricity supply would suffer significant setbacks if the situation persisted. item.title: Aguocha denies selling rice donated to Abia constituents
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The member representing Ikwuano/Umuahia Federal Constituency of Abia State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Obi Aguocha, has denied allegations that he diverted and sold two truckloads of rice donated to his constituents by President Bola Tinubu. A former Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs in Abia State, Chief Charles Ogbonna, had accused the lawmaker of diverting the rice and selling it in the market in connivance with his in-law. Ogbonna challenged Aguocha to sue him if the allegations were untrue. However, in a statement, Aguocha described the allegations as false, malicious and fabricated, insisting that neither he nor anyone acting under his direction diverted, converted or sold any truckload of rice or palliatives. He said all food relief items allocated to his constituents under the relevant appropriation provisions were distributed transparently and directly to the people through established and verifiable community-based channels. Describing the allegations as a smear campaign against him, Aguocha said his relationship with Ogbonna deteriorated after he cautioned the former commissioner against making what he described as unfounded allegations against Abia State Governor, Alex Otti. The lawmaker, who is seeking re-election in 2027, alleged that his political opponents had resorted to spreading false claims because they could not defeat him in a fair election. He accused them of attempting to damage his reputation and diminish his political standing ahead of the polls. “Beyond the obvious attempt at character assassination, this orchestrated campaign was deliberate in its design to incite my constituents to anger, hatred, and mob violence against my person and office. “In a challenging economic climate, falsely telling citizens that public palliatives meant for them were stolen and sold is a dangerous, reckless tactic calculated to trigger civil unrest and bodily harm,” he said. Aguocha vowed to institute legal action against Ogbonna and others allegedly involved in the accusations, adding that his legal team was already compiling evidence. He urged his constituents to remain calm and vigilant, insisting that the allegations would not distract him from his re-election bid in 2027. item.title: He’s a Northern kid — Sowunmi slams Baba-Ahmed for calling Tinubu ‘a failure’
item.description: By Bayo Wahab Segun Sowunmi, a chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and member of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, has described Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), as a “Northern kid” following his criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. Baba-Ahmed had described Tinubu as a failure, arguing that although the president inherited a poor country with weak institutions, poverty and insecurity, he had spent three and a half years in office without delivering the expected results. But Sowunmi, who spoke on Vanguard’s Politics Hub on Wednesday, faulted the PRP chairman’s assessment, questioning his criticism of the president and challenging Northern leaders to reflect on the region’s development. “That’s a Northern kid. What did I say? He’s a Northern kid. When you behave like a kid, you are a kid,” Sowunmi said. The PDP chieftain, who said he grew up and attended school in Kaduna, said he remained concerned about the North and its development. He questioned the outcomes of resources allocated to the region over the years, arguing that its leaders should examine their own responsibilities rather than focus solely on criticising the president. “All the resources that have been allocated to the North, where is the result?” he asked. Sowunmi also invoked the legacies of Nigeria’s former leaders from the region, including Tafawa Balewa and Ahmadu Bello, questioning whether they would be satisfied with the North’s present condition. He said leaders should be willing to confront the region’s challenges honestly instead of becoming “so loudmouthed” when criticising people from outside it. Describing Baba-Ahmed as a “rabble-rousing little rat”, Sowunmi added that the PRP chairman did not speak for the entire North. Asked whether he was worried that the criticism came from a Northern elder, Sowunmi said the forthcoming elections would provide a clearer indication of political support. “They can make their comments. We are going to the polls. Data would tell you that those that are the critical territorial commanders of votes, they know themselves,” he said. The convener of The Alternative also pointed to the influence of religious leaders and their followers in determining political choices, citing the case of Islamic cleric Ibrahim El-Zakzaky. He questioned whether El-Zakzaky and his followers would necessarily reject Tinubu, referring to the president’s reported provision of a private jet for the cleric to attend the funeral of his leader in Iran. Sowunmi contrasted this with the treatment El-Zakzaky and his family received from those he accused of harming them, arguing that political support could not be determined solely by the criticism of individual leaders. item.title: US revokes over 300,000 visas under Trump administration – Official
item.description: The administration of United States President Donald Trump has revoked more than 300,000 visas issued to foreign nationals, saying it has stepped up enforcement against people accused of criminal activity, immigration violations and other offences. According to Al Jazeera, the US Department of State disclosed the figure on Tuesday, claiming the administration had cancelled visas at a faster rate than any of its predecessors. “We are taking, and will continue to take, action to keep our borders, and our nation, secure,” the department said. A State Department official said most of the revoked visas were linked to criminal activity, public safety concerns, immigration violations, fraud, misrepresentation or information suggesting that the holders no longer qualified to enter or remain in the country. The official added that more than 4,000 visas were revoked over cases involving birth tourism, in which foreign nationals travel to the United States to give birth. According to the official, 25 per cent of the revocations were linked to assault and related offences, while 22 per cent involved driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Theft and substance abuse or distribution accounted for seven per cent each. Earlier on Tuesday, State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said the administration was targeting foreign nationals who had violated US laws, committed fraud or posed national security threats. “We have zero tolerance for foreigners here on visas who break the law, commit fraud or undermine our national security,” Pigott wrote on X. The latest figure represents an increase from the more than 175,000 visa revocations reported in August. In January, the department said it had cancelled more than 100,000 visas, describing the figure as a record at the time. item.title: RMAFC reviews Anambra’s ₦70bn request to tackle insecurity, erosion

The request, covering security, environmental management, healthcare, education, agriculture, solid minerals and tourism, is being examined by the commission’s Indices and Disbursement Committee. RMAFC’s spokesperson, Marian Yusuf, disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja on Tuesday. Presenting the request at the commission’s headquarters, the Secretary to the Anambra State Government, Chiamaka Nnake, said the proposed funding would help protect lives and livelihoods, restore investor confidence and accelerate economic growth. Nnake said Anambra, with 21 local government areas and 179 communities, had an estimated population of 8.9 million, a Gross Domestic Product of about $12.7 billion and a projected 2026 budget of ₦766 billion. item.title: Reforms Are Yielding Results, Okpebholo Urges Edo Residents To Back Tinubu’s Re-Election
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has appealed to residents of the state to support President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying the federal government’s economic reforms are beginning to show in development and better governance. Okpebholo appealed on Wednesday when he visited the Ojuromi of Uromi, HRH Zaiki Anselm Aidenojie II, at the traditional ruler’s palace in Esan Northeast Local Government Area. He was accompanied by members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), according to a statement by Chief Press Secretary to Okpebholo, Dr. Patrick Ebojele. Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, speaking on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, when he visited the Ojuromi of Uromi, HRH Zaiki Anselm Aidenojie II, at the traditional ruler’s palace, in Esan Northeast Local Government Area. Speaking on his administration’s record, the governor listed road construction, the upgrade of primary healthcare centers, regular payment of salaries, and the building of schools among the areas where work is ongoing. He admitted that much of what his government is doing will not show results overnight. “Most of the work I am undertaking can not manifest in one day. It takes time because it involves construction,” he said. “Many roads have been completed, and we have started several others in different parts of the state. They will ease movement and improve economic activities in Edo,” he said. Governor Okpebholo also spoke about electricity, one of the state’s long-standing challenges. He said a 100-megawatt power plant is expected to come on stream in Edo South in the near future, with another project to add 16 megawatts. “These projects are part of our efforts to address the power problem in the state,” he said. The governor credited the federal government for progress so far. “The man driving that success is Mr. President. That is why I am here to tell you that I do not want Edo to be in opposition to this government because of the progress we are already making,” he said. Earlier, His Royal Highness (HRH) Aidenojie II, Ojuromi of Uromi,speaking on behalf of the Esan Enigies commended the governor for his efforts at fast tracking development to the state. He prayed for God’s blessings and prayed that God would continue to give him wisdom to pilot the affairs of the state. Aidenojie, who described the governor as his son, assured him that the anticipated eight years of his administration would be completed. item.title: How To Protect Yourself From Ebola Infection
item.description: The Federal Government on Tuesday confirmed the first case of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Ebola is a disease that spreads through direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of an infected person or animal, according to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). ﻿ Following the confirmation, below are facts on transmission/causes, symptoms, and how to protect yourself and loved ones. How Does It Spread? Ebola can be spread through: Direct contact with blood, sweat, saliva, vomit, or other bodily fluids of an infected, symptomatic person Touching contaminated surfaces such as clothing, bedding, or other materials contaminated with fluids from an infected individual Consuming infected wild animals, handling deceased bodies without safety gear. Know The Symptoms Symptoms typically appear two to 21 days after exposure. The symptoms include: Fever Vomitting Headache Diarrhea Weakness/Fatigue Bleeding Muscle pain Sore throat How To Protect Yourself Wash hands regularly with clean running water and soap, or use alcohol-based sanitiser. Avoid contact with dead bodies and wild animals. Ensure all meat products are handled hygienically and thoroughly cooked. Do not touch bodily fluids of sick individuals or handle deceased bodies without professional health protocols. Health workers should adhere strictly to Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) standards. Myth Vs Facts Let’s set the record straight! Myth: Ebola spreads via casual contact (handshake, hugging). Fact: Ebola does not spread through casual contact. It requires direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person. Myth: Ebola spreads through food and water. Fact: Ebola does not spread through food and water, but all foods should be thoroughly cooked. Drink clean water always. Myth: Ebola spreads through the air. Fact: Ebola is not an airborne virus. Transmission strictly requires direct physical contact with bodily fluids or contaminated objects from a person showing active symptoms. Myth: Healthcare facilities are not safe during outbreaks. Fact: Healthcare facilities are strengthening infection prevention and control measures, including triage systems, hand hygiene, use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and isolation procedures to protect patients and healthcare workers. Stay informed and avoid panic. Spreading unverified rumours causes unnecessary fear and hampers response efforts. Always rely on official health updates. item.title: Ebola: We Have A Problem With Delayed Diagnosis, Resources To Cope — Medical Doctor
item.description: Delayed diagnosis and a dearth of essential medical resources continue to hinder Nigeria’s public health response more than the nature of the Ebola virus, a professor at the College of Medicine, University of Lagos, Dr. Alero Roberts, has said. ﻿ Roberts explained that the pathogen’s behaviour remains unchanged and predictable, adding that the real problem lies in systemic shortcomings and hesitation by members of the public, which she said compromises patient outcomes before medical intervention can begin. “I have no problem with the virus itself; the virus is doing what the virus does, it hasn’t changed its behaviour, and the virus is doing what the virus does,.” she said during an interview on Channel Television’s The Morning Brief on Wednesday, while reacting to Nigeria’s first confirmed case of the Bundibugyo strain of he virus. “We do have problems with the delayed diagnosis, seeking appropriate care and definitely with the availability of resources to cope.” The doctor also noted that no country in the world has the resources to manage the massive outbreak of the virus. “No country in the world today has the resources to cope with the massive outbreak of Ebola. Once the diagnosis has been made, Ebola becomes a nursing care issue, and there are just not enough nurses; kudos to the nurses, there are just not enough nurses to cope with the major outbreak of Ebola,” Roberts said. “Which is what we are seeing in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) already, so we must stick with prevention, border control, identifying, and as a public health physician I will be going with high index of suspicion to treat every patient as a possible case and initiate what we call the IPC ring. “The IPC ring is Infection Prevention and Control; we have got to initiate that because those are our first line of defense and they have proven very effective in the past,” she added. Speaking further on the breakfast show, Roberts said, “If you have been exposed but you do not have any symptoms, the good thing about Ebola is that you are not contagious. item.title: Macron Lands In Saudi Arabia On Surprise ‘Solidarity’ Visit
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron landed in Riyadh, where he is due to meet Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Wednesday, in a surprise “solidarity” visit after weeks of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Macron is the first Western leader to visit the kingdom since Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis intensified their attacks this month. The trip is part of a Gulf tour to secure diesel and petrol supplies as Macron seeks to bring down energy prices following violent protests in France sparked by rising living costs that have created a political crisis for the president. “The president of the republic is travelling to Saudi Arabia this afternoon to meet with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman,” a statement from Macron’s office said. The visit aimed to “demonstrate France’s solidarity with the kingdom in the face of the attacks carried out by the Houthis against its territory, and to continue efforts undertaken on securing and diversifying hydrocarbon supplies”, it added. France’s President Emmanuel Macron, flanked by Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani (L) and Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani, attends the 9th Annual One Planet Sovereign Wealth Funds (OPSWF) Summit at the Rosewood Hotel in Lusail on October 21, 2026. In recent weeks, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have reached an unprecedented scale, forcing Riyadh airport to shut and the postponement of a major investment conference. A Houthi attempt to blockade Saudi ports is also hampering oil exports from the kingdom.
